extracted.intended_audience: students and professional economists at all career stages (undergraduates, post-baccalaureate, graduate students, post‑docs, and faculty)
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional guidance describing NBER career opportunities and expectations across the academic career lifecycle, including undergraduate research, post‑baccalaureate and graduate research positions, fellowships, appointments as affiliated scholars, meetings/calls for papers, and conduct expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate research participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduates who are interested in pursuing careers in economics may apply to become involved in the NBER’s faculty-directed research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undergraduate research assistants may gather and analyze economic data, create charts and graphs, code, and check mathematical calculations. Reaching out to faculty members directly can often lead to research opportunities, both during the academic year and during the summer. See Projects and Centers for breadth of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-baccalaureate research positions (eligibility and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER provides opportunities for recent college graduates who are interested in pursuing graduate training to participate in research experiences that may guide them towards careers in economics. The NBER hires a number of full-time post-baccalaureate researchers each year to work with affiliated scholars on their research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-baccalaureate opportunities are listed on the Research Assistant Positions at NBER page. Besides positions at NBER, many NBER-affiliated scholars hire full-time post-baccalaureate research assistants at their home institutions. These positions typically last for one or two years and are often stepping-stones to graduate study. Opportunities are usually posted in the summer or early fall, with rolling deadlines throughout the fall and early winter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathways to Research and Doctoral Career consortium participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER is proud to participate in Pathways to Research and Doctoral Career, a consortium of universities and research institutions that aims to remove barriers to access to research and doctoral careers in the quantitative social sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities with the consortium partners can be found at predoc.org; this is a resource for predoctoral access and outreach rather than an NBER-specific hiring program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student research assistantships (hiring structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students in economics can participate in NBER activities in a number of ways. Many work as research assistants on projects directed by NBER-affiliated researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NBER does not maintain a centralized hiring program for these positions; affiliated researchers make hiring decisions, and interested students should contact individual researchers directly. These positions can develop research skills and may lead to opportunities to co-author papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation-writer fellowships (targeting and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER offers dissertation-writer fellowships targeted at graduate students working on particular topic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In recent years there have been programs in behavioral macroeconomics, energy economics, the economic effects of an aging workforce, and household finance. These fellowships are funded by federal agencies, private foundations, and the NBER itself. Fellowship opportunities are posted in the fall and typically begin the following academic year. Some pre-doctoral fellows work at the NBER’s office in Cambridge; many work at their home institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-doctoral fellowship expectations (residency & participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some fellowships provide support for post-doctoral scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In recent years NBER has offered fellowships for early-career scholars working on topics such as health and aging, long-term fiscal policy, and wealth inequality. Post-doctoral fellows are expected to be resident in Cambridge and to participate in the scholarly life at the NBER and the local economics community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship announcements and subscription
rubrics_metrics.description: Both pre-doctoral and post-doctoral fellowship opportunities are posted each fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The option to register for both pre- and post-doctoral fellowship opportunity announcements is available on the Edit Free Content Preferences page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of job listings for new PhDs (limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER does not maintain a systematic list of job opportunities for new PhDs, like the AEA Job Openings for Economists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A number of NBER-affiliated scholars hire post-doctoral researchers or fellows through their home institutions. The NBER maintains a centralized listing of these opportunities and other related positions, but not a comprehensive job market listing comparable to the AEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate appointment eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, following a highly competitive nomination and review process led by the directors of the 20 NBER research programs and advised by steering committees of leading scholars in each field, the NBER appoints about 60 new affiliated scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are currently about 1800 NBER-affiliated researchers. NBER affiliates may be Faculty Research Fellows, who are typically junior scholars, or Research Associates, who all have tenure at their home institution. All new affiliates must hold faculty appointments at North American colleges or universities. Affiliated researchers are invited to program meetings and may distribute research in the NBER working paper series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-funded research and Calls for Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: NBER-affiliated researchers may conduct grant-funded research under grants administered by the NBER. The NBER also periodically undertakes larger projects that fund a number of connected research projects by different groups of investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NBER will issue an open Call for Proposals for initiatives; research findings from projects under these initiatives are often presented at capstone conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research meetings: types, participation, and calls for papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER hosts more than 140 research meetings in a typical year, many of which — including the roughly 50 meetings that comprise the Summer Institute — post open calls for papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NBER hosts two types of meetings: program meetings that bring together researchers in a field of economics, and meetings focused on a specific topic. While participation in all meetings is by invitation, many researchers without NBER affiliations participate in both types of meetings. All economists, not just NBER affiliates, are invited to respond to open calls for papers. Calls may be found on the Calls for Papers page. Timing/example: Summer Institute had about 2,800 participants in 2025, with >500 first-time attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference code of conduct and expected behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBER is committed to providing a welcoming environment for the exchange of ideas at all of its research meetings. The Conference Code of Conduct underscores the institutional commitment to the fair treatment of all participants in a setting that is free of any kind of harassment or discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and meeting participants are expected to adhere to the Code of Conduct; the Code is the institutional standard governing behavior at NBER events.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find NBER opportunities (centralized listings and links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many NBER opportunities and related positions are listed on centralized NBER pages (Research Assistant Positions at NBER, Calls for Papers, centralized listing of opportunities and other related positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are directed to specific pages (Research Assistant Positions at NBER, Calls for Papers, Projects and Centers, Affiliated Scholars, Edit Free Content Preferences) and external resources (predoc.org) to find specific opportunities and announcements.
